title: What If Earth Had Rings Like Saturn?

scenes.text: What if Earth had rings like Saturn? They would never rise or set.
From Ecuador, a ring would look like a thin line standing straight up from the horizon.
From Washington, D.C., it would arch across the sky, visible day and night.
They'd be rock, not ice. Earth is so close to the Sun that sunlight would vaporize any ice.
Their shadows would darken one hemisphere each season, so winters might turn colder and harsher.
But the Moon's tides would likely tear them apart. Earth may have had one briefly, after the collision that made the Moon.

description:
What if Earth had rings like Saturn?
They would arch across the sky, cast seasonal shadows, and probably not last because of the Moon.
